title: Venom: Let There Be Carnage
edition: Original 2021 US PG-13 theatrical feature starring Tom Hardy
synopsis: An interview with Eddie gives imprisoned killer Cletus Kasady access to symbiote blood. As Carnage helps Kasady escape, Eddie and Venom quarrel and separate.
verdictRationale: Dan helps Anne rescue her former fiancé, and Eddie and Venom must repair their friendship to save her. Yet Venom injures Eddie, heals him and repeats the injury as a gag. Other hosts die during his night out with little attention to their loss. The pleasure the film takes in its hero’s cruelty weighs more heavily in this proposal than the reconciliation at the end.
ageRationale: A prison escape includes mutilation. A threatened execution, the murder of a priest and scenes recalling childhood abuse may trouble teens even when the effects look cartoonish.
reflection: Dan could treat Eddie’s trouble as a chance to keep a rival away. He supports Anne and comes to help. His freedom from jealousy gives a family a quieter example to take home than the cathedral fight.

themes.name: Reconciliation
themes.evidence: Eddie and Venom’s separation leaves Anne in danger. Their reunion makes her rescue possible.

themes.name: Generosity
themes.evidence: Dan repeatedly assists Anne and Eddie despite the romantic history. His help supports the rescue.

themes.name: Cruelty
themes.evidence: Carnage’s escape and the cathedral killings make lethal spectacle central. Even Venom hurts Eddie during a comic argument.

themes.name: Vengeance
themes.evidence: Frances pursues the officer who injured her. Retaliation follows her from captivity into the wedding.

themes.name: LGBTQ Themes & Messaging
themes.evidence: At a dance club, Venom uses a closet metaphor about leaving Eddie. ABC reads the speech as a coming-out allusion. The line identifies neither a human partner nor a character’s orientation. Check the theatrical cut for other explicit references before assigning film-wide prominence.

warnings.name: Spiritual material

warnings.name: Moral themes

questions: What does Eddie’s rule against eating people protect, and where does Venom still cause harm?

title: Venom: The Last Dance
edition: Original 2024 US PG-13 theatrical feature starring Tom Hardy
synopsis: A creature hunts Eddie and Venom for the Codex formed when Venom saved Eddie’s life. Keeping their bond intact could give Knull a path out of captivity.
verdictRationale: Venom finally accepts the loss of his life and his companionship with Eddie to protect others. That choice gives their friendship real weight. Earlier, the hero eats four men who mistreat dogs, and the scene treats their deaths as a satisfying punishment. Families have grounds to admire the farewell while questioning what the film invites them to enjoy along the way.
ageRationale: Creatures consume soldiers and spray blood. One survivor loses both legs. These images, a child’s death in a lightning flashback and strong language warrant older-teen guidance.
reflection: Venom once saved Eddie by joining himself to him. Here, love asks him to let Eddie go. An Orthodox family might consider the cost of giving another person a future one will never share.

themes.name: Self-sacrifice
themes.evidence: Venom gives up his bond and draws the attacking creatures to their destruction. The resolution depends on his choice.

themes.name: Cooperation
themes.evidence: Humans and symbiotes defend one another at the base after the military pursued them for much of the story.

themes.name: Retribution
themes.evidence: Venom decapitates the men involved in dog fighting. It is an early episode of lethal punishment by the hero.

themes.name: Domination
themes.evidence: Knull sends creatures to seize the Codex and free him. The resulting threat drives the pursuit to its end.

themes.name: LGBTQ Themes & Messaging
themes.evidence: The theatrical guide describes Eddie and Venom’s friendship. Its comparison to marriage also draws on advertising. Check the released film for explicit dialogue or relationships before assigning a film-wide score.

warnings.name: Sexual or suggestive content
warnings.details: Jokes reference male anatomy. A character wears a low-cut dress.

warnings.name: Language
warnings.details: Repeated swearing includes strong profanity and religious exclamations.

warnings.name: Violence and distress
warnings.details: Xenophages devour soldiers. A rescued soldier has lost both legs.

warnings.name: Spiritual material
warnings.details: Knull claims divinity and is presented as the maker of the symbiotes within the film’s fictional universe.

warnings.name: Alcohol
warnings.details: Venom mixes a drink for Eddie. Eddie describes feeling hungover.

warnings.name: Moral themes
warnings.details: Venom attacks men who exploit fighting dogs. Humans and symbiotes later risk their lives for one another.

themeScripture.text: Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.
themeScripture.connection: Christ’s words give families a way to discuss the cost Venom willingly bears for Eddie. The parallel concerns his gift of himself at the end of the film.

patristic.author: St. John Chrysostom
patristic.work: Homily 77 on the Gospel of John
patristic.section: Section 1, on Christ’s command to love
patristic.text: Because this is the mark of the disciples, this the bond of virtue.

biblicalParallels.title: A farewell that gives Eddie a future
biblicalParallels.filmMoment: Venom separates from Eddie and takes the creatures with him.
biblicalParallels.reflection: Christ’s words give families a way to discuss the cost Venom willingly bears for Eddie. The parallel concerns his gift of himself at the end of the film.

questions: Why does the Codex put the very bond that once saved Eddie in danger?
What response to the men running the dog fights could protect the animals and spare the men?
What changes when soldiers and symbiotes face the xenophages together?
What does Venom give up that Eddie cannot give back to him?
How does Eddie’s grief change the way you remember the pair’s earlier joking at the bar?
